construct.diagnosis_or_process: Alternating hemiplegia of childhood due to ATP1A3 dysfunction
construct.mechanism: ATP1A3 encodes a neuronal Na+/K+-ATPase alpha subunit. Pathogenic variants can produce alternating hemiplegia of childhood, with onset before 18 months, recurrent hemiplegic or quadriplegic episodes, dystonia/abnormal eye movements, developmental abnormalities, and a characteristic improvement or remission of attacks during sleep.
construct.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
construct.primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination

second_answer_attack.resolution: Hemiplegic migraine can cause episodic weakness, but onset before 18 months, alternating sides or quadriplegia, developmental/oculomotor abnormalities, and consistent remission with sleep are classic ATP1A3 alternating hemiplegia of childhood features.
